page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7ne.xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.3 GHz. The CPU architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. It does not include integrated graphics processing units or bundled local storage, requiring attached network block storage for operating system and data retention.

Benchmark results show mixed computational performance characterized by moderate single-threaded metrics and restrained multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core testing, place the instance within the mid-range tier, reflecting steady per-core clock frequency. However, multi-core throughput in stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests falls within lower benchmark quartiles due to the limited total core count of two physical cores. Memory throughput tests register 31.69 GB/sec for uncached read tasks and 25.55 GB/sec for write tasks, pairing with a Redis benchmark result of 3.98 million operations per second and static web throughput of 4.65 GB/sec.

From an efficiency perspective, ecs.g7ne.xlarge offers dedicated execution resources without the variability seen in shared-core models, though its processing density remains tailored to modest workloads. Given its balanced resource ratios and lack of local storage, the instance fits standard web application serving, continuous integration runners, lightweight caching nodes, and microservices that operate within moderate thread limits and standard network profiles.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7ne.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at 3.3 GHz. Configured with 16 GiB of memory, it maintains a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio suitable for balanced application workloads. Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16 instruction sets, along with AES cryptography support. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage for stateful operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate single-thread capabilities alongside lower relative throughput in multi-core and memory bandwidth tests, reflecting its constrained four-thread footprint. This configuration provides a cost-efficient resource tier for microservices, standard web hosting, lightweight development pipelines, and basic utility services that do not require high sustained multi-threaded execution or heavy I/O throughput.
